summary.text: Daughter of Pelias and Anaxibia (`anaxibia-pelias`) at Iolcus — one of the Peliades in Apollodorus' catalogue beside Pisidice, Hippothoe, Alcestis, and Acastus.
Homonym guard: not Pelopia daughter of Thyestes and mother of Aegisthus (`pelopia`). As a Peliad she belongs to the daughters whom Medea's cauldron deception led to boil their father Pelias.

story.text: Apollodorus names Pelopia among the daughters whom Pelias begot on Anaxibia, daughter of Bias — sister to Pisidice, Hippothoe, Alcestis, and their brother Acastus in the Iolcan royal stemma.

On Jason's homecoming Medea worked the ruin of Pelias through his own daughters: after the lamb sprang from the cauldron, they minced and boiled their father at her promise of restored youth — the vengeance that cleared the throne and set Acastus to bury Pelias and expel Jason and Medea.
